title: Carbon Pricing and Green Finance in Road Transport: A Bibliometric Analysis of Low-Carbon Transition Mechanisms
summary: Abstract In the face of the escalating climate crisis, the decarbonization of road transport and the transition towards a low-carbon economy have become strategic priorities for governments, particularly given the transport sector’s significant contribution to global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. In this context, carbon pricing and green finance have emerged as two complementary policy instruments capable of accelerating the sector’s transformation. Carbon taxation seeks to internalize the environmental costs associated with GHG emissions within economic decision-making, while green finance aims to mobilize the financial resources required to support sustainable development, enhance energy efficiency, and promote the adoption of lower-carbon mobility solutions. Despite the growing body of research in both fields, their interplay within the specific context of road transport decarbonization remains relatively fragmented in the scientific literature. This study is based on a systematic review of the scientific literature, primarily using the Scopus database to gather relevant publications on carbon pricing, green finance, and road transport. Bibliometric tools, notably VOSviewer, were employed to analyze and visualize keyword co-occurrence networks, author collaborations, and citation linkages to map the interactions among core concepts. The objective is to identify research trends, major contributions, and scientific gaps concerning the role of carbon pricing and green finance mechanisms in driving the low-carbon transition of the transport sector. The findings highlight a steady rise in academic interest regarding how fiscal instruments and sustainable investments support transportation decarbonization. Additionally, keyword and co-author networks reveal distinct research clusters focused on environmental governance, green economics, and sustainable transport development. These results underscore the critical importance of carbon pricing and green finance as key catalysts for transforming road transport systems. Keywords: Carbon pricing, carbon tax, green finance, climate finance, road transport, decarbonization, sustainability.

title: Technology Push or Demand Pull? Supply-Chain AI Spillovers and the Quality of Green Innovation Toward Sustainable Production in Chinese Listed Firms
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) diffuses beyond adopting firms into the wider production network, yet the direction and quality of these spillovers remain underexplored, an omission that matters because only high-quality green innovation advances genuine sustainable transformation. We ask how supply-chain AI spillovers shape the citation-weighted quality of firms’ green patents and whether technology-push and demand-pull channels carry equal weight. Building inter-industry AI exposure from a pre-sample (2012) input–output structure for 4963 Chinese A-share listed firms over 2011 to 2023, and identifying effects with a shift-share instrument, we find that AI exposure significantly raises green innovation quality. Upstream technology-push spillovers dominate downstream demand-pull spillovers on average, but the asymmetry is conditional on supply-chain structure: the upstream channel prevails when suppliers are concentrated, and the downstream channel re-emerges when they are dispersed. The effect concentrates in green invention patents rather than utility models and operates through embedded technology transfer rather than in-house R&D. Sequencing AI toward upstream, input–output-dense sectors offers a network-level lever for steering digital technology toward high-quality green innovation and a more sustainable production system.

title: DIRECTIONS FOR ENSURING SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT BASED ON GREEN INNOVATION AND TECHNOLOGICAL MODERNISATION
summary: The article examines directions for ensuring sustainable economic development in Uzbekistan based on green innovation and technological modernisation, using data from the Ministry of Energy and the National Statistics Committee. Solar and wind generation rose from 0.43 billion kWh in 2022 to more than 10.5 billion kWh in 2025, and the share of green generation reached 19.4% of total electricity output. At the same time, an estimated 23% decline in hydropower output highlights climate risks, and reaching the 54% target by 2030 requires green generation to grow by 29–31% annually. Evidence-based recommendations on green finance, energy efficiency, industrial modernisation, research and innovation, and regional development are proposed.

title: GREEN FINANCE AND CAPITAL CIRCULATION IN SMART AGRICULTURE: AI-DRIVEN INSIGHTS
summary: This scientific article examines the role of digitalization and smart agriculture in advancing green finance, AI-driven innovation, and inclusive rural investment. The main objective of the study is to assess how integrating digital technologies and AI systems into agricultural finance can enhance productivity and support sustainable community development. Drawing on the theoretical foundations of digital finance, green finance, and development policy, the research explores the relationship between traditional credit systems and innovative technological solutions to drive structural transformations in rural economies. The analysis shows that conventional agricultural finance mechanisms are often constrained by limited access to funds, high transaction costs, and insufficient risk management. Digital tools, including mobile banking, fintech platforms, and AI-based credit scoring, improve financial accessibility, optimize investment decisions, and increase transparency, while smart agricultural technologies enhance efficiency, productivity, and climate resilience. The study also discusses long-term trends in global agro-food trade and regional structural characteristics reflecting uneven import and export flows across regions. Overall, the research demonstrates that combining digitalization, AI, and targeted finance can significantly foster more sustainable and productive agricultural development, increasing both efficiency and financial inclusion while supporting long-term resilience in rural communities.

title: Governance Through Decision-Making Structure: a Driver of Corporate Social Responsibility in Cameroonian SMEs
summary: Abstract This article examines the influence of decision-making structure, understood as a formal mechanism of internal governance, on the social and societal practices of Cameroonian small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Drawing on stakeholder theory and resource dependence theory, the study posits that a more open, participative and diversified decision-making structure fosters responsible engagement toward employees and the local community. Data were collected through a questionnaire administered to fifty-two SME managers in the city of Douala and processed with SPSS (principal component analysis, Cronbach's alpha, simple linear regression). Results show that decision-making structure positively and significantly explains the social and societal practices of the SMEs studied (standardized beta of 0.735; R² of 0.541; F of 58.815; p < .001). These findings confirm the research hypothesis and are consistent with prior studies conducted in Cameroonian and African contexts. The article discusses these results in light of the existing literature and proposes managerial implications relating to the participation of middle managers and women in decision-making bodies, and to the delegation of managerial responsibilities within SMEs. Keywords: decision-making structure, corporate governance, corporate social responsibility, SMEs, stakeholders, Cameroon.

title: LAW AT THE GREEN–DIGITAL FRONTIER: Reimagining Ecological Justice, Sustainability, Economics and Technology in Emerging Environmental Governance
summary: Environmental governance is changing fast. Problems in the natural world keep growing. At the same time, money needs and new technology are moving ahead. Law is now pulled into this mix more than before. This work looks at a new area where environmental rules meet digital tools. In this space, environmental law is not only about traditional regulation but it also touches sustainability goals, fairness for affected communities, trade-offs tied to the economy, and fresh technology methods. The paper reviews how economic ideas help with sustainable development. It looks at the polluter pays principle, methods for valuing the environment, carbon markets, green finance, and ways to push environmental costs back onto those who cause harm. It then turns to new tools that are starting to matter. This includes artificial intelligence, remote sensing, satellite-based monitoring, blockchain, and systems that use environmental data to guide decisions. These tools may help with compliance checks, better tracking, clearer reporting, and more solid climate choices. It mentions the risk of bias in algorithms. It discusses who controls environmental data and how rules can be enforced fairly. It notes that new technology may not reach everyone in the same way. The paper puts ecological justice first. It also highlights fairness between generations. It stresses environmental rights and the concerns of people who are often left out. Purely legal changes may not be enough. Economic tools alone will fall short. Even technology by itself will not solve the whole issue. Instead, the paper calls for one joined approach. In that view, law, the economy, ecology, and technology must connect and work at the same time. It then looks at new legal areas that could support fresh ideas. The goal is to encourage change without harming nature. It also aims to protect fair distribution and long-term sustainability. In the end, the paper imagines a legal system that can respond as things shift. It would guide both the green transition and the digital transition. At the same time, it keeps human rights, environmental protection, and accountability as key parts.

title: CORPORATE STRATEGY TO HUMAN CAPITAL: THE ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND GOVERNANCE TRANSITION IN HOSPITALITY WITH A BIBLIOMETRIC APPROACH
summary: Within The Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework has become a defining paradigm in the transformation of the hospitality industry, shifting the focus from profit-oriented models to integrated sustainability and accountability systems. In this context, understanding how ESG research evolves and what dimensions dominate the discourse becomes increasingly important. The aim of this study is to analyse the development of ESG-related research in hospitality between 2009 and 2025, with particular attention to the transition from financial governance to human capital-oriented approaches. Despite the expansion of the field, the literature remains fragmented, characterised by conceptual ambiguity with Corporate Social Responsibility, inconsistent measurement practices, and limited integration of ESG dimensions within servicebased industries. The research is based on a bibliometric analysis of 987 publications indexed in the Web of Science database. The methodological approach combines performance analysis with science mapping techniques in order to identify publication trends, intellectual structures, and conceptual developments within the field. The results indicate a significant increase in research activity after 2019, accompanied by a shift in thematic focus. Earlier studies primarily emphasised financial performance, environmental efficiency, and external stakeholder perceptions. In contrast, recent research highlights the growing importance of employees as key drivers of ESG value creation. This reflects a redefinition of the Social dimension, which increasingly functions as an internal governance mechanism centred on employee engagement, well-being, and organisational behaviour. At the same time, the Environmental and Governance dimensions remain strongly interconnected through performance metrics and regulatory requirements, resulting in an imbalanced ESG structure. The internal social dimension is less standardised and insufficiently integrated into strategic decision-making processes. The study concludes that this imbalance limits the effectiveness of ESG implementation in the hospitality sector. The findings suggest that future development depends on the systematic integration of human capital considerations into governance frameworks, particularly in response to emerging European sustainability regulations. The contribution of the paper lies in identifying the internal social dimension as a key frontier of ESG research and in providing a structured overview of the field’s evolution, offering both theoretical clarification and practical relevance for sustainability-oriented management in hospitality.

title: Accounting Information Entropy–Resilience Theory: A Dynamic Theory of Accounting Information Quality Under Economic Shocks
summary: Accounting information has traditionally been evaluated through relatively static concepts such as relevance, faithful representation, earnings quality, disclosure quality, information asymmetry, and value relevance. These perspectives have generated substantial advances in accounting research, yet they provide limited theoretical explanation of how the informational properties of accounting systems evolve when firms encounter economic disturbances. This paper develops the Accounting Information Entropy–Resilience Theory (AIERT), a dynamic theoretical framework in which accounting information quality is conceptualized as a changing informational state rather than a fixed firm characteristic. The theory introduces two central constructs: Accounting Information Entropy, representing the degree of uncertainty, disorder, ambiguity, inconsistency, and informational instability contained in an accounting information environment; and Accounting Information Resilience, representing the capacity of that environment to resist, absorb, adapt to, and recover from disturbances while preserving economically useful information. The framework integrates information theory, accounting information economics, organizational resilience, dynamic capabilities, market microstructure, and economic decision theory. AIERT proposes that economic shocks can increase accounting information entropy, that entropy can exhibit persistence and nonlinear escalation, and that resilience determines the extent to which informational deterioration is absorbed or transmitted into economic decisions. The theory introduces resistance, recovery speed, recovery completeness, entropy persistence, critical entropy thresholds, hysteresis, informational equilibrium, and shock-amplification mechanisms. A dynamic state-space representation is developed to formalize these relationships. The paper advances seven theoretical propositions concerning shock sensitivity, resilience, nonlinear entropy dynamics, threshold behavior, recovery asymmetry, hysteresis, and economic consequences. It further distinguishes accounting information quality from accounting information resilience and argues that a high-quality information system in normal conditions may nevertheless exhibit low resilience under severe disturbance. The paper concludes by developing an empirical research agenda capable of testing AIERT and by outlining implications for accounting research, standard setting, auditing, corporate governance, investors, and economic policy.

title: Artificial Intelligence in ESG and Financial Reporting
summary: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming an enabling technology for the collection, validation, analysis and communication of environmental, social and governance (ESG) information and financial information. At the same time, expanding sustainability disclosure requirements are increasing the volume, variety and frequency of non-financial information that organisations must manage. This paper examines how AI can strengthen the relationship between ESG reporting and financial reporting by improving data processing, anomaly detection, disclosure preparation, forecasting, risk identification and digital reporting. The study uses a qualitative, descriptive and exploratory research design based on secondary sources, including international reporting standards, Indian regulatory publications and recent academic literature. Particular attention is given to IFRS S1, IFRS S2, the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Taxonomy, India's Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) framework and BRSR Core. The findings indicate that AI can improve reporting timeliness, consistency, scalability and decision usefulness, but its effectiveness depends on data quality, governance, explainability, human oversight, cybersecurity and clear accountability. AI should therefore be treated as a controlled reporting technology rather than an autonomous substitute for professional judgement. The paper recommends an integrated AI-enabled reporting architecture with strong data lineage, model governance, human review, assurance controls and ethical safeguards.

title: Do ESG Commitments Curb Tax Avoidance? Evidence from ASEAN Banks and the Moderating Role of Audit Quality
summary: This study investigates the performance of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) and earnings management (loan loss provisions) on tax avoidance measured using Effective Tax Rate (ETR) and Cash Effective Tax Rate (CETR) with audit quality as a moderator in the banking sector in ASEAN. Using panel data regression analysis and moderated regression analysis matching 101 banks with 707 bank-year observations, empirical results show that ESG performance has an adverse effect on tax avoidance, meaning that a high ESG score can reduce the potential for tax avoidance. Earnings management is positively associated with tax avoidance, especially when measured by ETR. Another important finding is the role of audit quality, which is driven by the involvement of the big four auditors, as a significant moderation variable. Audit quality reinforces the negative relationship between ESG and tax avoidance and weakens the positive relationship between Discretionary Loan Loss Provisions (DLLP) and tax avoidance. These results confirm the importance of external audit supervision in suppressing aggressive tax strategies. This research contributes to developing agency theory and legitimacy by showing how high-quality audits can drive ethical financial practices. Practically, this study recommends strengthening the role of professional auditors and integrating ESG indicators and audit quality in evaluating corporate tax behavior.

title: The Association Between Suppliers’ Digital Transformation and Focal Firms’ Green Innovation: A Supply Chain Information Processing Perspective
summary: Based on Information Processing Theory (IPT), this study examines the relationship between suppliers’ digital transformation (SDT) and focal firms’ green innovation (FGI) from a supply chain information-processing perspective. It identifies three boundary conditions—geographical distance, environmental regulation intensity, and analyst attention—and further examines their moderating roles in the relationship between SDT and FGI. A focal firm–year dataset of Chinese listed firms from 2008 to 2022 was constructed through data matching. A series of robustness checks were conducted to assess the robustness of the findings. The results indicate that SDT is positively associated with FGI, consistent with the proposed information-processing explanation involving information transmission and information integration across the supply chain. Moreover, this positive association becomes more pronounced as geographical distance decreases, environmental regulation intensity increases, and analyst attention rises. Supplementary analysis provides indirect evidence consistent with the proposed information-processing perspective. By systematically examining the relationship between SDT and FGI beyond organizational boundaries and developing an information-processing explanation involving information transmission and integration, this study highlights the role of supplier–focal firm interactions in green innovation, thereby contributing to the literature on the determinants of green innovation and information spillovers.

title: Green finance influences financial stability through nonlinear dynamics in BRICS countries with FinTech and financial development as complementary drivers
summary: Green finance is expanding rapidly across the BRICS economies, yet little is known about whether this expansion supports or strains their banking systems. This paper examines the relationship between green finance and banking stability, as measured by the Z-score, in Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa over 2005–2024. The question is whether that relationship is nonlinear and whether FinTech adoption and financial depth change the point at which it bends. What the paper adds to studies that treat these variables one at a time is a direct estimate of the curvature and a threshold expressed as a function of the two moderators rather than as a single number. A two-step system GMM estimator is applied to linear and quadratic specifications, the latter adding the square of green finance, as well as its interactions with FinTech development and financial depth. The quadratic model indicates an inverted U-shaped relationship: the linear term is positive (0.042), and the squared term is negative (− 12.603 × 10 −6 ), which places the unconditional turning point at about 1666 units of the green finance indicator, slightly above the sample mean. Both interaction terms are positive and significant, so the turning point moves to the right as FinTech adoption and financial depth increase (from roughly 2400 to 3870 units across the scenarios examined). Dumitrescu–Hurlin tests indicate two-way causality between stability and each of its determinants. Because the panel contains only five countries, the GMM results are read as indicative rather than definitive, and they are cross-checked against second-generation unit root, cointegration and structural-break tests that date the main shifts to 2008–2011 and 2021. Given the size of the panel and the unverified comparability of the green finance and FinTech series across countries, the policy message is conditional: green finance appears compatible with banking stability at the levels observed in most BRICS countries, but its marginal benefit shrinks at high levels. The room for safe expansion depends on the digital and financial infrastructure that accompanies it.

title: Digital capability and supply chain resilience in rural food tourism ventures: the role of food supply chain integration
summary: Introduction Rural food tourism ventures coordinate perishable local supplies, food-service operations and fluctuating tourist demand. How digital capability and food supply chain integration relate to resource-saving practices and enterprise-level resilience remains unclear. Methods A four-wave matched survey of 467 women operators was analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling, bootstrap tests of statistical indirect associations and an ordinal-estimator sensitivity analysis. Public user-generated content was analyzed separately to characterize platform discourse. Results Digital capability was positively associated with food supply chain integration and enterprise-level supply chain resilience. Integration was positively associated with both the low-carbon-oriented and resource-saving food practices index and resilience. The direct association between the practices index and resilience was not statistically significant. Bootstrap estimates supported the indirect association between digital capability and the practices index through integration, but not the serial indirect association extending to resilience. Only the resilience text classifier met the prespecified reporting threshold; the remaining labels were retained as exploratory semantic cues. Discussion The findings distinguish resource-saving practices from disruption resilience and identify supply chain integration as an organizational correlate of both. Future research should test these associations in probability-based and gender-comparative samples and validate reported practices against measured energy use, food loss and emissions.

title: Digital Green Bonds and ESG-Linked FinTech Platforms: Democratizing Sustainable Finance in Emerging Economies
summary: Convergence and digital finance and sustainability convergence has generated new institutional solutions, which comprise digital green bonds and ESG-linked FinTech solutions. They are not merely the financial products, but hypothetical constructions of the flow of financial resources, the democratization of the capital markets, the mechanisms of incorporating environmental and social governance into financial flows, and the restructuring of institutional standards in the emerging economies. This paper is devoted to building a theoretical perspective on these innovations, in the framework of the financial inclusion theory, the institutional innovation theory, and sustainability transition frameworks. It argues that digital green bonds and ESG-related platforms are transformational engines that increase participation, transparency, and bringing about systemic transitions towards low-carbon economies. The analysis puts these instruments into a wider argument of how these instruments are juxtaposed in the context of sustainable finance.

title: Leadership succession and corporate social responsibility in family firms
summary: This study investigates the impact of CEO succession on corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance in family firms. Drawing on socioemotional wealth perspective, we argue that CEO succession creates tension between financial accountability and non-financial objectives as successors seek to establish legitimacy and maintain organizational stability. During this period, successors are likely to prioritize financial accountability, organizational continuity, and family control, reducing attention to reputational objectives maintained through CSR. We further propose that external pressures, including peer firms’ CSR practices and media attention, moderate this relationship by increasing the legitimacy costs of reducing CSR engagement. Using data from Chinese family firms, we find that CSR performance declines significantly one to two years after succession. This negative relationship is stronger when external pressure is weak but is mitigated, and may even reverse, under stronger peer and media pressures. Our findings demonstrate how family firms balance financial and non-financial objectives during leadership transitions.

title: Ethnic diversity and its effect on audit lag
summary: This study investigates the effects of chief executive officer (CEO) ethnicity, audit committee ethnic diversity, audit tenure, and accounting financial expertise on audit delay in consumer non-cyclical (CNC) companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). Drawing upon the resource-based view (Barney, 1991) and expanding the demographic frameworks of prior literature (Harjoto et al., 2015), this research employs a quantitative methodology using panel data regression with a fixed-effect model (FEM) on 73 firms during the 2022–2023 period (146 firm-year observations). The empirical results reveal that CEO ethnicity, audit committee ethnic diversity, and accounting financial expertise are significantly and negatively associated with audit delay, effectively minimizing financial reporting lag. Conversely, audit tenure exerts a significant positive influence on audit delay, suggesting that prolonged auditor-client relationships may compromise independence and slow reporting. These findings offer critical practical insights for companies, regulators, and investors aiming to strengthen internal corporate governance mechanisms and optimize financial reporting efficiency in emerging markets. Future studies can extend this single-sector scope by investigating broader governance determinants across diverse industries.

title: Financial reporting quality and investment efficiency: the moderating role of audit quality
summary: Purpose This study aims to analyze the influence of financial reporting quality (FRQ) and audit quality (AQ) on firms’ investment efficiency (IE) within an emerging market context and to explore whether AQ acts as a moderating factor in the relationship between FRQ and IE. Design/methodology/approach This study uses panel data from 291 non-financial listed firms in Vietnam covering the years 2014–2023, totaling 2,910 firm-year observations. IE is measured as the residual from an investment model based on growth opportunities. FRQ is created from three measures based on accruals and revenue, along with a composite FRQ index. The models are estimated using feasible generalized least squares (FGLS) and the two-step system generalized method of moments (SGMM). Findings Both FRQ and AQ positively influence IE, with AQ demonstrating greater robustness under SGMM. The interaction between FRQ and AQ is statistically significant and negative, suggesting a partial substitution effect. Research limitations/implications FRQ measurement methods may be subject to estimation errors, and AQ is constrained to a binary Big Four audit firms proxy. Potential self-selection bias and limited generalizability remain considerations. Practical implications Firms not audited by the Big Four audit firms are encouraged to strengthen their FRQ through timely and predictive disclosures. Simultaneously, regulatory authorities should enhance their oversight of audit practices and of IFRS implementation. Social implications Improving FRQ and AQ fosters transparency and efficient capital allocation. Originality/value This study offers new evidence from Vietnam, demonstrating that FRQ and AQ serve as partly substitutive governance mechanisms in emerging markets.

title: Confronting Biodiversity Risk: Its Role in Shaping Corporate External Financing Choice
summary: ABSTRACT This paper investigates how biodiversity risk shapes corporate financing decisions. We propose a Financing Hierarchy Distortion framework, arguing that biodiversity risk amplifies information asymmetry and legitimacy costs, thereby pushing firms toward debt‐heavy adjustments. To empirically test this, we introduce a novel firm‐level Biodiversity Risk ( Brisk ) measure derived from textual analysis of corporate disclosures and link it to objective ecological data via Biological Diversity Endowment ( BDE ). Using Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2009 to 2023 and excluding those in financial and real estate sectors and with ST designations, we find that higher biodiversity risk increases reliance on both formal and informal debt, particularly short‐term debt. These findings are robust to quasi‐causal identifications using difference‐in‐differences and instrumental variable strategies. Mechanism and heterogeneity analyses further corroborate the proposed framework and show that this distortion is more pronounced among firms in biodiversity‐dependent industries and those facing stronger institutional pressures. These adjustments, however, impose tangible economic costs, raising debt financing costs and depressing returns on assets. Overall, our findings highlight the unintended financial consequences of biodiversity risk, with policy implications for biodiversity disclosure standards, biodiversity‐linked financing instruments and the development of alternative credit channels to strengthen firm resilience under escalating ecological pressure.

title: AI in supply chain risk assessment: a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
summary: Abstract Supply chain risk assessment (SCRA) is pivotal for ensuring resilience in increasingly complex global supply networks. While existing reviews have explored traditional methodologies, they often neglect emerging artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) applications and mostly lack combined systematic and bibliometric analyses. This study addresses these gaps by integrating a systematic literature review with bibliometric analysis, examining 1,903 articles (2015-2025), with 54 studies selected through PRISMA guidelines. Our findings reveal that ML models, including Random Forest, XGBoost, and hybrid approaches, significantly improve risk prediction accuracy and adaptability in post-pandemic contexts. The bibliometric analysis identifies key trends, influential authors, and institutional contributions, highlighting China and the United States as leading research hubs. Practical insights emphasize the integration of explainable AI (XAI) for transparent decision-making, real-time data utilization, and blockchain for traceability. The study underscores the necessity of dynamic strategies, interdisciplinary collaboration, and continuous model evaluation to address challenges such as data quality and interpretability. By synthesizing AI-driven methodologies with resilience frameworks, this review provides actionable guidance for optimizing supply chain risk management, fostering adaptability, and informing future research in evolving risk landscapes.

title: Audit delay across ASEAN-5 economies: The role of audit characteristics, corporate governance, and institutional context
summary: Type of article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study aims to investigate the determinants of audit delay among real estate and property companies listed on ASEAN stock exchanges during the 2020–2025 period. Although the timely issuance of financial reports is important for attracting investor confidence and helping firm transparency, prior empirical evidence on the determinants of audit delay in the ASEAN context remains inconclusive. Drawing on Agency Theory, Signaling Theory, and Institutional Theory, this study examines whether audit fees, profitability, audit tenure, audit opinion, audit committee expertise, auditor reputation, and firm size influence the existence of audit delay.This study uses panel data from Refinitiv Eikon and company annual reports, including 254 companies and 1,524 company-year observations. A Random-Effects Logistic Regression model, which accounts for the panel data structure and unobserved heterogeneity across companies, is used for hypothesis testing because the dependent variable is dichotomous.The findings conclude that while profitability, audit tenure, and audit committee skill do not significantly influence audit delay, audit fees, audit opinions, auditor reputation, or firm size do. These results suggest that audit-process variables are more important in predicting audit timeliness than corporate governance procedures or performance characteristics.By providing cross-national empirical data from the ASEAN region, this study contributes to the expanding literature on audit delays. Additionally, by enhancing audit quality and implementing more efficient financial reporting procedures, the findings provide regulators and industry professionals with useful recommendations to improve financial reporting timeliness.AcknowledgmentThe authors gratefully recognise the financial assistance provided by the Institute for Research and Community Service (LPPM), Universitas Andalas, under the Flagship Research Scheme (PUJK), Batch I, through Contract No. 295/UN16.19/PT.01.03/PTM/2024. title: Green intellectual capital and green performance in Islamic higher education: the mediating role of green innovation
summary: This study aims to explore the mediating role of Green Innovation on the relationship between Green Intellectual Capital and Green Performance in Islamic Higher Education. Primary data was collected through a questionnaire from leaders/strategic managers at Muhammadiyah and Aisyiyah Universities (PTMA). The number of respondents in this study was 313. Green Human Capital does not directly impact Green Performance. In other words, the existence of individual environmental knowledge and competencies does not automatically translate into institutional environmental performance. Meanwhile, Green Innovation does not mediate the relationship between Green Relational Capital and Green Performance. This means that external relations in the context of Islamic higher education are more legitimacy-driven than innovation-driven. This research provides a policy roadmap for IHE leaders to develop GICs. Furthermore, this research can guide resource allocation toward a portfolio of green innovations that directly improve cost efficiency and reduce emissions. The originality of this research lies in its contextualization within IHE, an ecosystem with a mandate for scientific and moral outreach, distinct from general universities and business entities. Furthermore, the operationalization of GI mediation in a campus setting is not merely an intervening variable, but rather a measurable, dynamic capability.

title: Justifying membership fees through quality and pricing in a competitive supply chain
summary: While membership-based retail has experienced substantial growth, how membership stores can justify membership fees through product quality remains underexplored from a supply chain perspective. This study examines a supply chain consisting of a manufacturer, a membership store, and a traditional retailer, where consumers differ in their perceived value of exclusive membership services and may exhibit the sunk cost effect generated by the prepaid membership fees. We investigate how this behavioural mechanism affects retail pricing and the manufacturer’s quality investment. The results show that the sunk cost effect not only reshapes the membership store’s pricing strategy but also affects the manufacturer’s quality investment decision, thereby enabling the membership store to justify its membership fee. The equilibrium outcomes are jointly determined by the membership store’s competitive advantage and the perceived membership fee. Based on these two dimensions, we derive a strategic decision matrix comprising four equilibrium regimes. We use several business cases to help understand how membership stores can adjust their quality and pricing decisions according to their specific characteristics to justify membership fees. This study thus translates analytical results into a managerial framework and provides managerial insights for membership stores’ strategic decision-making.

title: Pengaruh Leverage dan Profitabilitas terhadap Manajemen Laba pada Perusahaan Manufaktur di Bursa Efek Indonesia
summary: Earnings management is an important issue in financial reporting because it can reduce the quality of financial information used by investors, creditors, and other stakeholders in making decisions. Leverage and profitability are frequently examined as factors that may influence management’s tendency to engage in earnings management. However, previous studies have reported inconsistent findings. This study aims to examine the effect of leverage and profitability on earnings management in manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange through a literature review approach. The study reviews scholarly articles obtained from Google Scholar and published between 2024 and 2026. Articles were selected using purposive sampling based on inclusion and exclusion criteria, resulting in 31 articles for analysis. Data were analyzed using content analysis by comparing previous findings to identify patterns, inconsistencies, and research gaps. The results show that the effect of leverage on earnings management remains inconsistent, with studies reporting positive, negative, and insignificant effects. Profitability also produces mixed findings, although most studies indicate a positive relationship with earnings management. These differences may be attributed to variations in research objects, observation periods, measurement proxies, and analytical methods. This study provides an overview of previous findings and identifies research gaps for future research.

title: Digital Transformation of the Procurement Function and Sustainable Performance of Private Logistics and Warehousing Firms in Nairobi County, Kenya.
summary: Digital transformation has become a strategic imperative in modern organizations, particularly within procurement functions, where the integration of digital tools, data systems and agile processes enhances efficiency, transparency and accountability. In Kenya, procurement accounts for about 10–13% of GDP, yet although more than 80% of public entities have implemented platforms such as IFMIS, only about 52% use them consistently, and logistics and warehousing firms continue to face low system utilization, inadequate technical skills, unreliable infrastructure and weak alignment between digital strategies and procurement objectives. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to examine the influence of digital transformation of the procurement function on sustainable performance of private logistics and warehousing firms in Nairobi County, Kenya. It specifically examined the effects of digital strategy alignment, technological capabilities, data-driven proficiency and process agility on sustainable procurement performance. The study was anchored on the Resource-Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the Technology Acceptance Model and Institutional Theory. A descriptive and explanatory research design was adopted, targeting 1,250 active logistics and warehousing firms in Nairobi County, with procurement officers, supply chain managers, ICT personnel and operations managers as the units of observation. A sample of 93 firms was determined using Nassiuma's formula and selected through purposive and stratified sampling, with one respondent per firm. Primary data were collected using a structured questionnaire, and both descriptive and inferential statistical methods, namely Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis, were used to analyse the data, which were presented in tables and discussed. The findings revealed that the four dimensions of digital transformation jointly explained 46.5% of the variation in sustainable procurement performance. Technological capabilities had the strongest positive and significant effect, followed by data-driven proficiency and digital strategy alignment, while process agility had a positive and significant but comparatively modest effect. The study, therefore, recommends that firms should upgrade ICT infrastructure and strengthen system integration and platform reliability, invest in analytics tools and staff training in procurement analytics, fully integrate procurement policies with digital transformation frameworks, and streamline procurement workflows to eliminate task duplication, so as to enhance sustainable procurement performance in logistics and warehousing firms in Nairobi County.

title: Mekanisme Tata Kelola terhadap Kualitas Laba: Peran Moderasi Kecepatan Publikasi Laporan Keuangan
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of audit committee independence and external audit quality on earnings quality, with financial statement publication speed as both a direct variable and a moderating variable. Earnings quality is measured using discretionary accruals via the Modified Jones Model. Using a quantitative causal design and purposive sampling, 15 mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2021–2025 were selected, yielding 75 observation data points. Data were analyzed using panel data regression with the Random Effect Model (REM) and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) in EViews. The empirical findings show that audit committee independence and external audit quality do not have a significant direct impact on earnings quality, indicating that internal governance structures and audit firm reputation often operate merely as regulatory compliance. Conversely, publication speed positively and significantly affects earnings quality, supporting signaling theory that timely financial reporting conveys transparent operational information. Furthermore, publication speed does not moderate the impact of audit committee independence on earnings quality, but it significantly weakens the relationship between external audit quality and earnings quality. This indicates that excessive time-budget pressure arising from accelerated publication deadlines compromises audit thoroughness, thereby diminishing audit quality effectiveness in curbing earnings management.

title: Inhibiting factors in digital supply chain implementation: Technology, organization, and environment framework study of the stilt-house industry in Tomohon City
summary: Digital transformation has reshaped supply chain management, yet adoption among small, traditional enterprises remains uneven. This study analyzes the factors inhibiting Digital Supply Chain (DSC) implementation among stilt-house (rumah panggung) producers in Tomohon City, a wood-based craft industry of cultural significance in North Sulawesi. A qualitative exploratory case study was analyzed through the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework. Data came from eight informants (four owners, two employees, one timber supplier, one customer), selected purposively, through participant observation, semi-structured interviews, and documentation, and were analyzed with the Miles–Huberman–Saldaña interactive model, with source and technique triangulation. DSC implementation remains simple and not integrated: electric machinery in production, smartphones in marketing, and phone calls and WhatsApp in procurement operate as isolated applications. Barriers appear in all three TOE contexts: cost, limited electrical infrastructure, and unavailable equipment (technology); comfort with conventional systems despite adequate basic competence (organization); and supplier distance and unmet expectations of government support (environment). Informants consistently reported benefits from the technology in use, so barriers constrain the depth and integration of adoption rather than negate its value. The case also suggests, as an interpretation, that some manual work (e.g., hand-carving) persists as valued craft practice rather than an unmet digital need, qualifying deficit-based readings of traditional industries.

title: ECONOMETRIC ASSESSMENT OF THE IMPACT OF DIGITAL ECONOMY DEVELOPMENT ON ECONOMIC GROWTH IN UZBEKISTAN
summary: This study empirically examines the impact of digital economy development on economic growth in Uzbekistan using annual time-series data from 2000 to 2023. Given the rapid structural transition of the Uzbek economy, the research evaluates whether consumer digital adoption (internet penetration and mobile cellular subscriptions) has yielded statistically significant short-term macroeconomic returns. Preliminary Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) unit root testing revealed severe nonstationarity in physical capital formation (>I(2)), explicitly invalidating standard cointegration techniques such as ARDL bounds testing.

title: Impacts of the digital economy on industrial employment and CO2 emissions: a comparison between developed and developing countries
summary: This article assesses the impact of the digital economy on industry and the environment by comparing 15 countries (7 developed and 8 developing) over the period 2000–2021. Using the System Generalized Method of Moments (SYS-GMM), the analysis reveals contrasting results between country groups. For developed countries, a 1% increase in ICT imports is associated with a 0.159% reduction in CO₂ emissions (p-value < 0.01) and a marginal 0.038% decrease in industrial employment (p-value < 0.10), consistent with automation-driven labor reallocation toward high-value-added sectors. In developing countries, the same 1% increase in ICT imports yields an insignificant effect on CO₂ emissions (− 0.008, p-value = 0.676) and industrial employment (− 0.016, p-value = 0.113), reflecting structural constraints including outdated energy infrastructure and limited absorptive capacity for green technologies. Industrial value-added positively influences employment in both groups, though the elasticity is higher in developed economies (0.048 vs. 0.031). The results underscore the need for developed countries to sustain investments in advanced digital infrastructure and innovation policies that accelerate the green digital transition. For developing countries, priorities should include strengthening green digital infrastructure, fostering international technology-transfer partnerships, and implementing targeted workforce retraining programs to maximize the employment and environmental co-benefits of digitalization.

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Organisational Performance: Examining Supply Chain Resilience in Manufacturing Firms and Strategic Decision-Making in Indian Start-ups
summary: Most firms no longer ask whether to use artificial intelligence (AI); they ask where it pays off first. This paper looks at two places where the answer seems clearest and the mechanisms quite different: supply chain resilience (SCR) in manufacturing, and strategic decision-making (SDM) in Indian startups. Drawing on the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities theory and organizational information processing theory (OIPT), we argue that AI matters less as a piece of automation and more as an added layer of information-processing capacity. In manufacturing that capacity shows up as earlier warning, steadier inventory and faster rerouting when something breaks. In startups it shows up as cheaper experiments, tighter control of cash and clearer signals about when to change course. The paper is conceptual and draws on published empirical work rather than new primary data. We set out a framework, compare the two settings, and offer a phased adoption roadmap with governance guidance. We also flag the claims that still need testing, because the evidence base, particularly for Indian startups, is thinner than the enthusiasm around it.

title: Firm-specific trade policy effect uncertainty and the bullwhip effect
summary: Purpose In an era of increasingly volatile trade policies, firms confront heightened uncertainty in demand forecasting and production planning, raising the potential for amplification of the bullwhip effect (BWE). Drawing on the BWE literature and on regulatory focus theory, which distinguishes between a promotion focus oriented toward gains and a prevention focus oriented toward loss avoidance, this paper investigates how firm-specific trade policy effect uncertainty (TPEU) influences the BWE, and how managerial regulatory focus moderates this effect. Design/methodology/approach Based on a sample of 37,017 firm-year observations from 4,104 publicly listed Chinese firms between 2002 and 2022, we employ ordinary least squares (OLS) regressions to test the proposed hypotheses. Findings We find that TPEU significantly amplifies the BWE. This effect is exacerbated in firms led by promotion-focused top management teams (TMTs) and attenuated in firms led by prevention-focused TMTs. Mechanism analyses reveal that TPEU affects the BWE primarily through firms' operational adjustments on both the demand and production, as well as through broader supply chain restructuring. These results are robust to a series of empirical strategies designed to address potential endogeneity concerns. Research limitations/implications The study focuses on publicly listed Chinese firms and relies partly on textual measures derived from corporate disclosures. Accordingly, the findings may not fully generalize to firms operating in other institutional and trade policy environments, and the measures may partly reflect managerial disclosure choices. Future research could test and extend the proposed relationships through cross-country comparisons, alternative measures of trade policy effect uncertainty and managerial regulatory focus, and more granular operational data. Practical implications The findings suggest that firms should treat TPEU as an important source of operational instability. Managers should strengthen demand forecasting and policy monitoring, avoid excessive ordering and inventory adjustments, and manage customer and supplier restructuring carefully. Firms should also consider how TMT regulatory focus shapes operational responses to uncertainty and balance opportunity-seeking with risk-avoidance in supply chain decision-making. Social implications The study shows that trade policy uncertainty can generate operational consequences that extend beyond individual firms by amplifying demand and production variability and disrupting customer and supplier relationships. Such amplification can propagate through interconnected supply chains, potentially weakening overall supply chain stability during periods of trade policy change. The findings therefore highlight the broader social and economic value of improving firms’ ability to absorb policy-related uncertainty, maintain stable supply chain relationships and avoid unnecessary operational overreaction, thereby supporting more resilient supply chains in an increasingly uncertain global trade environment. Originality/value We contribute to the emerging literature on the intersection of operations and supply chain management and trade policy uncertainty by documenting the operational consequences of trade policy-induced uncertainty, and by underscoring the critical role of managerial regulatory focus in shaping operational responses to TPEU.

title: A resource-based strategic management in Sharia banks: Examining the association of organizational culture, innovation, and digital transformation
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractSharia banking institutions in Indonesia have significant growth potential, given that the majority of the population is Muslim. This study aims to analyze the association between organizational culture, innovation, and digital transformation within the context of resource-based strategic management in Sharia banks of East Java. Data were collected from state-owned (6 main and 90 branch offices) and private (3 main and 66 branch offices) Sharia banks in East Java during January and February 2026, after these Sharia banks completed their annual financial reports. A total of 165 respondents were selected using a purposive sampling method. The selected respondents were secretaries with at least three years of work experience. Data were analyzed using structural equation modeling partial least squares (SEM-PLS). The analysis results show that organizational culture has a positive and significant relationship with resource-based strategic management (path coefficient = 0.450; t = 8.640; p < 0.001). Innovation also has a positive and significant relationship with resource-based strategic management (path coefficient = 0.305; t = 5.742; p < 0.001). Similarly, digital transformation has a positive and significant relationship with resource-based strategic management (path coefficient = 0.349; t = 6.183; p < 0.001). These findings indicate that organizational culture, innovation, and digital transformation are positively related to resource-based strategic management in Sharia banks of East Java.

title: LABOR MARKET SEGMENTATION IN THE CONTEXT OF THE DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF THE ECONOMY
summary: This article examines current trends in labor market segmentation in the context of the digital transformation of the economy. It explores the main criteria for labor market segmentation, the characteristics of internal and external labor markets, as well as the impact of digitalization and platform employment on the employment structure. The paper analyzes labor shortages, skill mismatches, and regional disparities. Particular attention is paid to the development of digital forms of employment, changing requirements for workers' professional competencies, and the transformation of labor relations. The article highlights the need to improve public policy in the field of labor market regulation, human capital development, and the adaptation of the vocational education and training system to current economic conditions.

title: Digital Transformation and the Relationship between Service Users and Public Administration
summary: Abstract This study examines how service users perceptions of digital transformation, access to information and waiting times relate to their perceived relationship with public administration in Morocco. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire distributed via LinkedIn and in person at several public administrations. Of the 146 people who responded, the 122 with complete answers on the model variables were retained for the regression analysis, The 14 measurement items cover four constructs, whose factorability and internal consistency were checked with Kaiser–Meyer–Olkin and Bartlett tests and Cronbachs alpha 0.725 to 0.811. A multiple linear regression explains 55.3% of the variance in the perceived relationship “adjusted R² = 0.542”. Perceived digital transformation β = 0.475, p < 0.001 and perceived reduction in waiting times β = 0.245, p = 0.003 are positively and significantly associated with the outcome, whereas the coefficient for access to information is positive but not significant at the 5% level (β = 0.135, p = 0.074). For these respondents, the quality of the relationship with the administration appears to depend more on visible changes in how services are delivered, including the time they take, than on information alone. Because the design is cross-sectional and relies on self-reported perceptions, the findings describe associations rather than causal effects. title: ESG e desempenho financeiro: uma revisão sistemática da literatura baseada em análise de conteúdo
summary: O objetivo deste trabalho foi realizar um mapeamento teórico da relação entre as práticas ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance) e os indicadores econômicos e financeiros das empresas. Para isso, foi realizada uma pesquisa de abordagem qualitativa, com objetivos exploratórios e descritivos, apoiada por técnicas quantitativas de análise textual. Para a seleção dos artigos, foi realizada uma Revisão Sistemática da Literatura (RSL) no período de 2019 a 2023, seguindo o método Systematic Search Flow (SSF), e a abordagem analítica dos dados foi conduzida por meio de análise de conteúdo, utilizando a análise de nuvem de palavras, análise de similitude e a Classificação Hierárquica Descendente (CHD), realizadas com o apoio do software Iramuteq. Os resultados permitiram apontar que os principais indicadores econômicos e financeiros identificados foram o indicador econômico Q de Tobin e os indicadores financeiros Retorno sobre o Ativo (ROA) e Retorno sobre o Patrimônio Líquido (ROE). Esses indicadores estão relacionados com a sustentabilidade e as práticas ESG. Contudo, foi observado também que não há consenso na literatura sobre a relação entre ESG e desempenho financeiro. Os indicadores identificados são ferramentas que podem ser utilizadas por todos os stakeholders, facilitando a tomada de decisões mais estratégicas. Para gestores e investidores, a compreensão desses indicadores é importante, pois permite uma avaliação que vai além do retorno econômico e financeiro imediato, incorporando também os riscos e oportunidades ligados às práticas sustentáveis.

title: IS GREEN FINANCING PROFITABLY REWARDING AND BOOST MARKET VALUATION? A COMPARATIVE STUDY ON INDONESIAN BANKS
summary: This research investigates the financial and market implications of green financing adoption within the Indonesian banking sector (2019-2024). While many argue that green projects entail higher risks, this study posits that high commitment to green financing yields superior performance. Using an Independent Sample Ttest, we compared 108 observations divided into two groups: High Green Financing (High GF) and Low Green Financing (Low GF) intensity. The results demonstrate a significant disparity in both operational and market performance. Banks in the High GF category achieved a significantly higher Return on Equity (Mean = 13.39%; p < 0.001) compared to their counterparts (Mean = 6.64%). Furthermore, market valuation, proxied by Tobin’s Q, was significantly higher for the High GF group (Mean = 1.08 vs 0.99; p = 0.02). These findings suggest that green financing is not merely a corporate social responsibility burden but a strategic driver that enhances internal profitability and attracts market premium. This study provides empirical support for the "doing well by doing good" hypothesis in the context of Indonesia's emerging sustainable finance landscape.

title: Smart City Pilot Programs and the Advancement of the Digital Economy: Empirical Insights from China
summary: Abstract In recent years, China has experienced rapid urbanization and technological advancement, with particular emphasis on the development of smart cities. A smart city integrates advanced technologies to enhance overall efficiency, improve the quality of urban services, and foster economic development. As part of this broader trend, various Chinese cities have initiated smart city pilot programs to explore the potential benefits of integrating digital technologies into urban management. Against this backdrop, this article seeks to assess the impact of smart city pilots on the development of the digital economy in China. Based on panel data from 285 Chinese cities at the prefecture level or above between 2011 and 2019, this article employs a difference-in-differences method to evaluate the impact of smart city pilots on the development of the digital economy. The research findings indicate that on average, smart city pilots significantly enhance the level of digital economy development by 0.756%. Smart city pilots can affect the development of the digital economy through mechanisms such as digital consumption, information collection, and human capital. These conclusions provide significant policy references for accelerating the construction of smart cities and promoting the development of the digital economy in China in the new era.

title: Communication of Succession Intent and Corporate Governance in Family-Owned SMEs in Uganda’s Central Region
summary: Communication of succession intent and corporate governance are critical determinants of sustainability in familyowned enterprises.This study examined the clarity of succession strategies, employee engagement, and role alignment, mediated by governance practices, to assess their influence on the sustainability of selected family-owned SMEs in Uganda's central region.The study adopted a mixed-method exploratory design, combining quantitative survey data with qualitative interviews to capture both statistical relationships and contextual insights.Quantitative data were collected from 166 respondents using structured questionnaires, while qualitative insights were obtained through key informant interviews.Findings revealed that clarity of succession communication moderately enhanced transparency (M = 3.199, SD = 1.151), while employee awareness (M = 3.711, SD = 0.874) and role alignment (M = 3.922, SD = 0.623) strongly reinforced confidence and continuity.Regression results confirmed that succession communication significantly predicts sustainability (β = 0.362, R² = 0.337, p < 0.001), while corporate governance emerged as an even stronger predictor.Qualitative evidence highlighted emotional reluctance and informal practices as barriers, with leaders admitting, "everything is in my head," yet positive examples emphasized merit-based transparency.The study concludes that transparent communication, reinforced by governance, reduces uncertainty, mitigates conflicts, and transforms succession planning into a structured, accountable system.Recommendations include formalizing communication strategies, institutionalizing open forums, integrating succession into performance reviews, and strengthening governance frameworks to ensure resilience and long-term sustainability of familyowned SMEs in Uganda.

title: Pengaruh Inventory Intensity, Capital Intensity dan Corporate Governance terhadap Manajemen Pajak
summary: This study aims to determine the effect of *Inventory Intensity, Capital Intensity,* and *Corporate Governance*, proxied by Independent Commissioners, on tax management, both partially and simultaneously. This study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data in the form of financial statements of the companies selected as research objects. The sampling technique used is *purposive sampling*, which involves selecting samples based on predetermined criteria in accordance with the research objectives. The collected data were analyzed using EViews Version 12 through several statistical testing procedures to examine the relationships and effects between the independent and dependent variables. *Inventory Intensity* is used to measure the level of a company's investment in inventory, while *Capital Intensity* reflects the proportion of the company's investment in fixed assets. Meanwhile, *Corporate Governance* is proxied by Independent Commissioners as one of the company's monitoring mechanisms. The results show that *Inventory Intensity, Capital Intensity,* and *Corporate Governance* partially have an effect on tax management. The simultaneous test results also indicate that *Inventory Intensity, Capital Intensity,* and *Corporate Governance* collectively have an effect on tax management. These findings indicate that corporate decisions related to inventory, fixed assets, and corporate governance play an important role in determining a company's tax management strategies.

title: THE IMPACT OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON THE ECONOMIC EFFICIENCY OF ENTERPRISES IN UZBEKISTAN
summary: This article examines the impact of digital transformation and the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies on the economic efficiency of enterprises in Uzbekistan. It analyses the mechanisms through which digital technologies affect labour productivity, cost optimisation, innovation activity and managerial decision-making. The study employs statistical, comparative and systems analysis methods. Drawing on official statistical data for Uzbekistan, it assesses trends in the development of digital infrastructure and proposes a composite indicator for measuring the effectiveness of digital transformation at the enterprise level.

title: Digital Transformation in the Textile Cutting Sector: An Industry 4.0 Approach to Operational Excellence
summary: Purpose – This study investigates how the integration of Industry 4.0 monitoring technologies with structured change management and employee involvement can improve FCI system adoption, operational data quality, and warehouse efficiency in the cutting department of a Portuguese textile SME. Design/methodology/approach – Action research methodology was employed across four iterative phases – problem identification, action planning, implementation, and reflection – at ATêxteis S.A., a knitwear manufacturer. Data collection triangulated direct observation, FCI/ERP system logs, anonymous employee questionnaires, and supervisor interviews. Theoretical grounding draws on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Kotter’s eight-step change model. Findings – FCI system registrations increased nearly three-fold (300 to 1,000 per month) between November 2022 and July 2023, with registrations per 1,000 pieces cut rising from 3.5 to 12.2. Remnant warehouse occupancy decreased from 28.35% to approximately 15% of total capacity. ERP integration enabled automatic detection of material consumption discrepancies, and quality non-conformance detection increased from an estimated 5–8 to 23 cases per period. Results confirm that change management and participatory training are the proximate drivers of digital tool adoption, even when system use is formally mandated. Originality – The study provides rare empirical evidence on Industry 4.0 implementation in textile SME cutting operations, extending TAM and Kotter’s model to a manufacturing digitalization context. It introduces a production-normalized utilization metric (registrations per 1,000 pieces) and demonstrates the complementarity of Lean principles with digital monitoring for operational excellence in traditional manufacturing.

title: Toward an Audience‐Based View of Incumbent Adoption of Potentially Discontinuous Technologies: Evidence From Fintech
summary: ABSTRACT We advance an audience‐based view of incumbent adoption of potentially discontinuous technologies. Drawing on theories of discursive institutional processes and categorical legitimacy, we model how incumbents navigate mixed judgments from external groupings in their environment, that is, audiences, when adopting prospective discontinuous technologies. We argue that incumbents filter this noisy discursive environment by factoring in audiences' credibility and authority. We develop contextualized hypotheses and test them on a longitudinal sample of 149 incumbent financial firms responding to the emergence of financial technology in Europe from 2000 to 2016, distinguishing industry insiders, support experts, the general public, and regulators. Uniform engagement across audiences has a non‐linear influence on adoption. Incumbents respond most visibly to judgments from the general public and resist positive engagement from support experts. Industry insiders' and regulators' engagement did not have robust direct linear effects. Our findings reveal a preparadigmatic legitimacy puzzle wherein conventional institutional predictions systematically fail or reverse when legitimacy signals remain contested across audiences. We develop four propositions theorizing the expertise penalty, democratic legitimacy under uncertainty, authority without clarity, and temporal heterogeneity of audience influence, establishing the need to differentiate between audiences to understand incumbent responses in the preparadigmatic phase of technology evolution.

title: Supply chain security and global dependencies in the trade of phosphorus-related products
summary: Phosphorus (P) is fundamental to all living organisms and serves as a non-substitutable nutrient in fertilizers, yet its global supply largely depends on phosphate rock (PR) mining concentrated in a small number of countries. In 2023, global PR mining reached 220 million tonnes, with approximately 93% used for fertilizer production. Driven by population growth and rising animal-product consumption, P-fertilizer demand is projected to increase by 40% by 2060 relative to 2020 levels. Combined with low recycling rates and uneven resource distribution, these trends heighten the risk of future supply disruptions and pose geopolitical challenges. This study analyzes global phosphorus flows and trade dependencies from 2001 to 2023 using a mass-flow-based trade network, tracing PR from extraction to final fertilizer while enhancing supply chain resilience. The results show that supply dependencies extend beyond mining countries and are structurally embedded in transformation and trade networks. Morocco and Jordan account for around 50% of global PR outflows, while China dominates phosphorus transformation in downstream categories. Countries without PR reserves, including Belgium, Germany, Spain, and The Netherlands, emerge as critical trade and transformation hubs. This concentration of mining, transformation, and trade creates systemic supply security risks, particularly for inflow-dependent countries such as Pakistan and Indonesia, whose inflows rely on a limited number of suppliers. The findings reveal hidden interdependencies that amplify vulnerability to supply disruptions. Addressing these via diversification and transparency enhances supply chain resilience.

title: THE GOVERNANCE-PERFORMANCE NEXUS IN AN EMERGING MARKET: ANALYSING BOARD EFFECTIVENESS, OWNERSHIP STRUCTURE, AND EXTERNAL ASSURANCE IN NIGERIA
summary: This study investigates the relationship between corporate governance and stock marke performance in Nigeria by developing an integrated governance triad comprising board effectiven ownership structure, and financial reporting oversight. Unlike previous Nigerian studies that predominantly examine individual governance mechanisms in isolation, the study considers their combined relevance within an emerging-market institutional context. Using an ex post facto correlational research design, the study analyses an unbalanced panel of 112 non-financial firms li: on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX) over 2013-2022. The dataset contains 986 firm-year observations, while the dynamic System GMM estimation reports 874 usable observations after application of the lag structure and estimation requirements. Stock market performance is primari measured using Tobin's Q, with market capitalization growth employed as a robustness measure. I effectiveness is measured through board independence, board size, and board activity; ownership structure through ownership concentration, institutional ownership, and foreign ownership; and financial reporting oversight through Big Four auditor affiliation and audit committee financial exp The study employs a two-step System Generalized Method of Moments (System GMM) estimator address dynamic endogeneity and unobserved firm heterogeneity. The findings indicate that boar independence has a positive and statistically significant association with firm value, while board si: board activity are insignificant. Ownership concentration exhibits a significant inverted U-shaped relationship with firm value, with the estimated turning point at approximately 67.6%. Institutiona ownership is positive and significant, whereas foreign ownership is insignificant. Audit committee financial expertise is positive and significant, while Big Four auditor affiliation has no standalone significant association with firm value. Robustness estimates using market capitalization growth pr broadly consistent results, and the reported Big Four x audit committee financial expertise interac indicates that audit quality is more valuable where competent internal financial reporting oversigh exists. The study concludes that the Nigerian market appears to place greater value on substantive governance capacity than on formal governance signals considered in isolation. The findings have implications for regulators, corporate boards, and investors seeking to strengthen governance effectiveness, minority-shareholder protection, and market confidence in Nigeria.

title: THE EFFECT OF ESG, FREE CASH FLOW, AND CORPORATE GOVERNANCE ON FINANCIAL DISTRESS
summary: Objective- This study aims to analyze the influence of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG), Free Cash Flow, and Corporate Governance on Financial Distress in non-cyclical consumer sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2022–2024 period. Financial distress is a condition in which a company experiences a decline in its financial health and difficulty meeting its financial obligations, which can be an early indication of bankruptcy. In recent years, ESG implementation, the ability to generate free cash flow, and good corporate governance have become important concerns because they are considered capable of supporting a company's stability and long-term sustainability. This study employed a quantitative method with a panel data approach. Purposive sampling was employed to select 93 companies with a total of 279 observations. The research data consisted of secondary data obtained from annual reports and company sustainability reports. Financial distress was measured using the Altman Z Score model, and ESG was measured using the Sustainability Report Disclosure Index (SRDI) in accordance with the 2021 GRI Standards. Free cash flow was calculated using operational cash flow and capital expenditures, while corporate governance was measured using 15 corporate governance indicators. Data analysis was performed using E-Views 12 software. The results of the study show that ESG, free cash flow, and corporate governance do not have a significant effect on financial distress. Findings- This shows that the level of ESG disclosure, the company's ability to generate free cash flow, and the implementation of corporate governance have not been able to optimally reduce the risk of financial distress in non-cyclical consumer sector companies. Limitations- This research is limited to a research scope that only covers one company sector, and the use of independent variables are still limited. Originality-This study examines the factors that influence ESG, Free Cash Flow, and Corporate Governance in finding evidence of whether there is a risk of Financial Distress.

title: Promoter share pledging and insolvency reform: a creditor rights perspective
summary: Given the 2016 Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) reform in India, the interplay among promoter share pledging (PSP), firm leverage, and profitability is crucial for understanding the impact of these reforms on corporate financing behaviour and the power dynamics between creditors and promoters. This study examines whether the IBC altered promoter financing behaviour by changing the relationship between firm leverage, profitability, and PSP, thereby addressing the limited evidence on how creditor-rights reforms affect PSP among financially vulnerable firms. Using panel data from 2011–2020 covering pre- and post-IBC periods, we employ a difference-in-differences (DID) approach as a quasi-natural experiment to identify the reform’s effects. Our study found that the IBC strengthened the impact of leverage intensity on PSP, as highly leveraged firms increased share pledging following the reform, particularly those with lower profitability, as indicated by the significant negative triple interaction. The findings contribute to the literature on promoter financing behaviour and creditor rights by showing that the response to insolvency reform differs according to firms’ leverage and profitability, with implications for creditor monitoring and corporate governance.

title: Global logistics in a changing environment and best practices implementation
summary: The international economic interdependence and transnational organization of goods and services with global supply chains determine the economy, environment and working conditions in many countries around the world in numerous ways. The main risks in the supply chain are of an economic, ecological, political and ethical nature. The EU Supply Chain Act obliges companies to operate fairly and sustainably and to respect human rights and ecological protection in their supplier network. This contribution describes the effects of geopolitical hazards on the tactical level of the supplier network. Challenges include costs, disruption and regulatory and compliance issues. A case study of an automotive manufacturer shows supply security and resilient supply chains; risk management in purchasing, e.g. internal manufacturing, Innovations as a strategical competitive edge; digitalisation; social and environmental responsibility and carbon emissions.
