title: Distributional heterogeneity in the effect of green innovation on carbon emissions across G20 economies
summary: This study investigates whether green innovation reduces carbon dioxide emissions in G20 economies over 1985–2024. It develops a diagnosis-driven empirical strategy in which estimator selection follows formal tests for cross-sectional dependence, slope heterogeneity, integration, and cointegration. The results reveal strong cross-sectional dependence, reject slope homogeneity, and show that heterogeneity is driven largely by a small number of influential economies, particularly India and Türkiye. Long-run relationships are estimated using the mean-group estimator and the outlier-robust trimmed mean-group estimator. Conventional mean-group estimates are largely statistically insignificant, whereas the trimmed estimator delivers precise estimates of all five long-run coefficients, highlighting the importance of outlier-robust aggregation in heterogeneous panels. The preferred results trace an inverted-U income–emissions profile. A one-percentage-point increase in the renewable-energy share is associated with a 0.032-ton long-run decline in per-capita emissions, and a doubling of renewable-energy patenting with a 0.051-ton decline. Panel quantile regression with common shocks shows that the innovation effect is distribution-dependent. The effect is statistically indistinguishable from zero in low-emission conditional states, and it strengthens monotonically toward the upper tail. At the 90th percentile, a doubling of patenting is associated with a reduction of roughly 0.065 tons. These findings identify renewable-energy deployment as a distribution-wide decarbonisation lever and green innovation as a targeted one, operating where emissions are highest.

title: Pengungkapan ESG dan Nilai Perusahaan Sektor Energi dengan Kinerja Keuangan sebagai Mediator
summary: This study examines the direct and indirect associations between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure and firm value through financial performance among Indonesian listed energy companies. A quantitative study used annual and sustainability reports for 44 firms over 2022–2024, yielding 132 firm-year observations. Disclosure was scored by reported items, financial performance was measured by return on assets (ROA), and firm value by Tobin’s Q. Panel regressions were estimated using random effects for the ROA equation and fixed effects for the firm-value equation; indirect effects were assessed with the Sobel test. Environmental and social disclosure were not significantly associated with ROA, whereas governance disclosure had a negative association (coefficient −0.099451; p = 0.0203). In the firm-value equation, environmental disclosure was positively associated with Tobin’s Q, social disclosure negatively associated, governance disclosure not significant, and ROA positively associated. The reported Sobel statistics indicated no significant indirect effect for the environmental or social dimensions, but a significant negative indirect effect for governance through ROA. The findings show that combining ESG dimensions into one score may conceal distinct directions and channels. Investors should assess disclosure alongside profitability and the quality of underlying practices. The observational design and short study period limit causal and long-term interpretation.

title: THE IMPACT OF GOOD CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, BOARD GENDER DIVERSITY AND OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY ON BANKING FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE
summary: This study is motivated by the fluctuating financial performance of banking companies in Indonesia during the research period. This condition reflects inconsistencies between the implementation of corporate governance, board gender diversity, and operational efficiency toward company profitability. This study aims to analyze the effect of Good Corporate Governance (GCG), Board Gender Diversity, and Operational Efficiency on financial performance proxied by Return on Assets (ROA). The research objects are banking companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2020–2024 period. This research employs a quantitative approach with an associative research design. The data used are secondary data obtained from companies’ financial statements and annual reports. The sample was determined using purposive sampling techniques, while the analytical method applied is panel data regression. The research testing includes selecting the best model, conducting classical assumption tests, and hypothesis testing. The results indicate that partially, Good Corporate Governance and Board Gender Diversity do not have a significant effect on Return on Assets (ROA). Meanwhile, Operational Efficiency has a significant effect on the financial performance of banking companies. Simultaneously, all independent variables significantly affect financial performance. The findings suggest that operational efficiency is the dominant factor in improving banking profitability. The implementation of corporate governance and board gender diversity still require optimization to provide a more substantial contribution to financial performance improvement.

title: Assessment of barriers to lean, green, and digital innovations in net-zero supply chain with an integrated MCDM approach
summary: Abstract Rapid industrialisation and increased online purchases have significantly increased the carbon footprint of supply chains (SCs), necessitating the transition towards net-zero SCs. Though lean, green, and digital (LGD) innovations have demonstrated potential to impact the net-zero SC transition, their adoption remains limited in emerging economies due to several barriers. Evaluation of the significance and interrelationships of the barriers remains elusive in the existing literature, highlighting the need for systematic investigation. Accordingly, this study aims to identify, evaluate, and prioritize the barriers to the adoption of LGD innovations in an emerging economy to facilitate the transition toward net-zero SCs. A systematic literature review was performed to identify barriers to incorporating LGD innovations, and principal component analysis with 345 respondents was employed to finalise the same. The finalised barriers were analysed using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) methods in the Fermatean Fuzzy System (FFS) context. The outcomes suggest market competition (0.5641), the absence of a sustainable vision and goal (0.5489), the dilemma over the resilience of LGD innovations (0.5429), the absence of appropriate policy mechanisms (0.5418), and the lack of stakeholder support (0.5400) as the five most critical barriers. The study's implications could help SC practitioners make decisions related to net-zero emissions, potentially reducing adverse environmental impacts. The uniqueness of this work lies in the integration of FFS with AHP and DEMATEL to evaluate the barriers to integrating LGD innovations into SC activities.

title: SOCIAL COMMERCE AND SME COMPETITIVENESS: ENHANCING FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: This study examines the role of social commerce in improving the competitiveness and financial performance of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in the digital economy. The rapid development of digital technology, especially social media platforms, is gradually changing the way businesses interact with customers and run their operations. For SMEs, this shift opens up opportunities to reach a wider market, improve efficiency, and build closer relationships with customers at relatively low costs. This study uses a qualitative approach based on a literature review of previous studies related to social commerce adoption, SME competitiveness, and financial performance. The findings show that the use of social commerce tends to increase product visibility, encourage customer engagement, and support sales growth. These improvements can contribute to better financial performance and business sustainability. Additionally, features such as live streaming, user-generated content, and online reviews have been found to influence consumers' purchasing decisions. However, SMEs still face several challenges, including limited digital literacy, limited resources, and ongoing platform algorithm changes. This condition can affect how effectively social commerce is used in practice. Therefore, it is important for SMEs to continue to adapt and strengthen their digital capabilities to remain competitive. In conclusion, social commerce plays an important role in supporting the competitiveness of SMEs and financial performance. With the right strategy and the right use of digital platforms, SMEs can achieve more sustainable growth in an increasingly competitive environment.

title: Intelligent planning and scheduling system for supply chain logistics routes based on reinforcement learning
summary: The optimization of logistics routing and scheduling in supply chains is a critical challenge, particularly in dynamic environments characterized by fluctuating demand, traffic conditions, and stringent time-capacity constraints. Traditional optimization methods and heuristic-based approaches often struggle to adapt and maintain stability in non-stationary settings. Reinforcement learning models, while promising, face limitations in scalability, sensitivity to reward variance, and generalization under dynamic conditions. This research proposes the Dynamic Actor-Critic Proximal Policy Optimization (DACA-CPPO) framework to address these challenges. The Dynamic Actor-Critic algorithm (DACA) component improves policy and value adaptation by dynamically updating the actor and critic networks, while the Clipped Proximal Policy Optimization (CPPO) stabilizes policy updates through clipping, ensuring that the policy updates remain within a stable range and preventing large, destabilizing changes. The framework is evaluated using a dataset of 32,065 records with 26 features, split into 80% for training and 20% for testing. Data preprocessing techniques, including Z-score normalization and feasibility filtering, ensure consistent scaling and valid state transitions across training and testing sets. Node2Vec-based graph embeddings are employed to extract spatial and topological features of logistics networks, while statistical and temporal variables such as demand, capacity utilization, and scheduling urgency are incorporated into the state representation. The results show that the DACA-CPPO framework achieved 95% accuracy, reduced delivery costs, lowered delay rates, and improved route efficiency compared to baseline reinforcement learning strategies. Implemented in Python, the framework offers a stable, scalable, and adaptive solution for optimizing logistics planning in dynamic, real-time environments. Not applicable.

title: Generative AI in supply chains: a qualitative study on decision-making and human-AI collaboration
summary: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has recently gained attention as a technology that supports supply chain decision-making due to its unique natural language capabilities. In this context, it is seen as a top-layer augmentation to traditional analytical and optimisation-based technologies, accelerating decision support needed to keep businesses competitive. While extant literature largely discusses the conceptual potentials of GenAI, empirical evidence on its implications for human-AI collaboration and its boundaries with other AI technologies remains limited. Therefore, the present study adopts an abductive qualitative approach to explore GenAI-based decision-making through semi-structured interviews with experts. The empirical data were analysed using thematic analysis and subsequently interpreted through the lens of a recent AI decision-making framework. By theorising the empirical insights, this study clarifies GenAI’s current role as a cognitive decision-support layer rather than an autonomous decision-maker, along with its limitations. The findings contribute to the literature by providing empirical validation of GenAI as an augmentative technology and by offering evidence-based guidance on how organisations can responsibly leverage GenAI to enhance decision quality, operational efficiency, and operational resilience.

title: Forensic Accounting and the Doctrine of Criminal Intent in Financial Fraud: A Legal and Audit-Based Examination of Mexico’s Oceanografía–Banamex Case
summary: Financial fraud in receivables financing presents challenges for identifying documentary manipulation, tracing financial responsibility, and assessing evidence of criminal intent. This study develops an integrated forensic accounting and legal assessment framework to examine Mexico’s Oceanografía–Banamex case, focusing on the relationship between financial irregularities, authorization practices, and evidence relevant to deliberate deception. The framework combines transaction reconstruction, invoice verification, documentary triangulation, transaction network analysis, and an evidence matrix to distinguish indicators of intentional misconduct from negligence and weaknesses in internal controls. The study dataset comprises 12,000 receivables financing records, 2,400 invoice documents, 180 authorization logs, and 60 correspondence files covering a three year observation period. Data preparation involves record standardization, duplicate identification, chronological alignment, and reconciliation of invoices with financing and approval information. Twenty four forensic indicators assess unsupported receivables, repeated invoices, inconsistent approval dates, unusual financing concentrations, documentary discrepancies, and authorization exceptions. Rule based screening and network analysis identify potentially irregular transactions, which are subsequently assessed against reference labels through independent documentary review. Legal analysis organizes the resulting evidence according to its relevance to knowledge, deception, participation, and financial benefit, while considering alternative explanations. The integrated framework identifies 912 of 960 labelled irregular records, achieving 95.0% recall. Among 1,000 flagged records, 912 correspond to reference irregularities, yielding 91.2% precision and a 93.1% F1 score. Conventional checklist screening identifies 720 irregular records, producing 75.0% recall. The proposed approach therefore improves recall by 20 percentage points, demonstrating stronger identification of irregular financing patterns within the analyzed dataset. Documentary inconsistencies and recurring authorization exceptions provide priorities for further investigation, although these indicators alone cannot establish criminal intent or individual guilt. The study contributes an auditable framework connecting financial analysis with legally relevant evidentiary assessment. Its findings support integrated verification, transaction tracing, and contextual review as complementary tools for investigating complex financial fraud. The framework emphasizes evidence provenance, document authentication, corroboration, and distinctions between suspicious transactions and established responsibility. Its practical value lies in strengthening investigative prioritization and audit transparency while supporting carefully qualified legal interpretation of financial evidence within the examined case context.

title: The Dual Synergistic Effect of Digital Policies: How Data Factorization and Technological Intelligence Co‐Shape Corporate ESG Performance
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines how the synergy between data factorization and technological intelligence affects corporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance using comprehensive panel data from Chinese A‐share listed companies (2007–2024). Leveraging the staggered establishment of National Big Data Comprehensive Pilot Zones and National Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Application Pilot Zones as a well‐identified quasi‐natural experiment, we provide causal evidence that policy synergy significantly enhances corporate ESG performance, with this composite effect notably surpassing any single‐dimensional pilot policy. Net effect tests further reveal that while building artificial intelligence upon an established big data foundation yields a significant marginal premium over isolated AI policies, this synergistic dividend is not instantaneous. Mechanism tests reveal that the policy synergy improves corporate ESG performance through two core channels: the technology empowerment effect and the governance optimization effect. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that policy synergy effects are more pronounced in domestic enterprises, core digital economy industries, and nonheavily polluting sectors. Additionally, the transmission efficiency of policy dividends is positively moderated by favorable internal resource endowments and external institutional pressures yet inhibited by severe financial constraints. Further analysis demonstrates an optimal temporal sequencing pattern consistent with dynamic complementarity theory: following a “factor accumulation first, intelligent application second” implementation logic, with synergy dividends peaking when artificial intelligence policies supplement big data policies after approximately 3 years. This study advances the literature by moving beyond single‐policy evaluation to identify the causal effects and temporal laws of policy complementarity, revealing the micromechanism of digital policy synergy driving corporate value creation and providing important empirical support for government optimization of the temporal sequencing and spatial layout of digital economy governance systems.

title: The Digital Lever: How Can Digital Intelligence Transformation Drive Urban Green Innovation?
summary: The digital and intelligent transformation of urban development has sparked new reflections on green innovation in cities for the new era. China’s national big data comprehensive pilot zone policy provides a practical arena for exploring this issue. This study, based on panel data from 287 prefecture-level cities in China from 2011 to 2022, examines the mechanisms through which the national big data comprehensive pilot zone policy affects urban green innovation. The results show that the pilot zone policy significantly improves the level of urban green innovation, with the level of digital economic development and the intensity of environmental regulation being important mediating pathways, forming a dual path of technology-driven and institutional synergy. Based on the empirical analysis results, the study proposes a “digital lever” framework to explain the combined effects of policy foundations, digital empowerment, and environmental regulation.

title: Generative AI risk prediction capability and cross border agricultural trade resilience: a PLS-SEM empirical study of coastal Chinese enterprises
summary: Introduction Maritime transport carries the predominant share of cross-border agricultural trade, and geopolitical conflicts, climate anomalies, port congestion, and proliferating trade barriers have intensified uncertainty for the coastal enterprises that depend on seaborne logistics. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers new pathways for building resilient supply chains through multi-source data fusion and risk prediction capabilities. However, empirical evidence examining how GenAI risk prediction capability (GenAI-RPC) relates to cross-border agricultural trade resilience (CATR) remains scarce. Grounded in the resource-based view (RBV) and dynamic capability theory, this study develops a direct-effects model linking three GenAI-RPC dimensions---multi-source cross-border risk identification and scoring, prediction accuracy and anti-hallucination stability, and AI risk model calibration and decision empowerment---to CATR. Methods Using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), we analyzed survey data from 300 agricultural enterprises engaged in cross-border trade across four coastal Chinese provinces (Shandong, Guangdong, Fujian, and Zhejiang). Results The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity: Cronbach's α ranged from 0.817 to 0.855, composite reliability from 0.880 to 0.902, and average variance extracted (AVE) from 0.623 to 0.697. All heterotrait-monotrait (HTMT) ratios were below 0.85, supporting discriminant validity. The structural model showed that all three GenAI-RPC dimensions were positively associated with CATR: multi-source risk identification ( β = 0.291, p < 0.001), prediction accuracy ( β = 0.251, p < 0.001), and model calibration ( β = 0.287, p < 0.001). The model explained 46.1% of the variance in CATR ( R 2 = 0.461; Stone--Geisser Q 2 = 0.112), with SRMR = 0.069 indicating acceptable fit. Among the control variables, enterprise digital transformation maturity showed a strong positive association with CATR ( β = 0.577, p < 0.001), and all three GenAI-RPC dimensions remained statistically significant after controlling for it. Discussion These findings contribute to the theoretical integration of GenAI capabilities with maritime supply chain resilience research and offer practical guidance for coastal agricultural enterprises and policymakers seeking to strengthen the resilience of seaborne food trade.

title: QUANTITY SURVEYORS AS ENABLERS OF ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND GOVERNANCE INTEGRATION IN THE MALAYSIAN CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRY
summary: The increasing emphasis on sustainability in the Malaysian construction industry highlights the importance of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) practices as a structured approach to sustainable development. As a major contributor to Malaysia’s economic growth, the construction sector faces growing pressure to balance economic performance with ESG considerations. This study explores the evolving role of Quantity Surveyors (QSs) as enablers of ESG practices in the Malaysian construction industry. ESG indicators from the FTSE Russell ESG Scores published by Bursa Malaysia were used to examine the alignment between ESG principles and QS professional practices across construction stages. A qualitative approach was adopted through semi-structured interviews with six middle-management professionals from contractor firms. The findings reveal that QSs contribute significantly to ESG implementation through green procurement, occupational safety and health (OSH), and ethical governance. However, implementation is constrained by resistance to change, supply chain limitations, reporting challenges, project characteristics, and limited client support. The study highlights the need for stronger governance, digital solutions, incentives, standardized ESG reporting, and greater involvement of professional bodies.

title: Layering of Controls: MCS Transformation in a Hybrid Public Accounting Firm
summary: Background: This study introduces layering of controls as a longitudinal and cumulative pattern in the transformation of Management Control Systems (MCS) within professional service firms. Objective: Unlike redesign or archetype-change perspectives, which treat MCS transformation as substitutive, this research demonstrates how new controls accumulate without replacing existing ones. The study draws on a single-case, longitudinal investigation of a non-Big Four Indonesian public accounting firm affiliated with a global network, observed across nearly four decades of organizational growth. Methods: Methodologically, the research combines eight years of participant observation by an insider partner-researcher (2017–2025), semi-structured interviews with six purposively selected informants reflecting maximum variation across hierarchy and background, and analysis of organizational documents, with reflexivity and triangulation employed to mitigate insider bias. Results: The findings reveal four sequential layers: founder-based personal and cultural controls, action controls through global audit methodology, formal governance, and integrated audit technology. Each layer reinforces rather than supplants the preceding layers. Conclusion: The study contributes by extending the MCS-as-package framework with a temporal dimension, explaining how intrinsic motivation sustains cultural control in professional firms, and showing that global affiliation in a hybrid model strengthens, rather than erodes, local strategic authority in emerging-market audit firms.

title: Green Strategic Management and Organizational Performance of Manufacturing Firms in Cross River State, Nigeria
summary: This study examined the effect of green strategic management on the organizational performance of manufacturing firms in Cross River State, with particular reference to Flour Mills Nigeria PLC, Calabar. Specifically, it investigated the effects of green innovation, green supply chain management and green human resource management on organizational performance. A descriptive survey research design was adopted. The population comprised 396 employees, from whom 196 respondents were selected through simple random sampling. Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire validated by experts in business management and research methodology. The instrument recorded an overall Cronbach’s alpha coefficient of 0.887, confirming its reliability. Of the 196 questionnaires administered, 184 were completed and returned, representing a response rate of 93.9 per cent. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis with SPSS version 27 at the 5 per cent significance level. The findings showed that green innovation had a positive and significant effect on organizational performance (β = 0.341, t = 5.679, p < 0.001). Green supply chain management also had a positive and significant effect (β = 0.377, t = 6.103, p < 0.001), while green human resource management exerted a positive and significant effect (β = 0.296, t = 4.754, p < 0.001). Collectively, the variables explained 69.1 per cent of the variation in organizational performance. The study concluded that integrating environmental considerations into innovation, supply chain activities and human resource practices significantly improves overall organizational performance. It recommended cleaner technologies, environmentally responsible sourcing and regular employee environmental training.

title: Effect of Financial Attributes on Value of Listed Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria
summary: The value of a firm remains a central concern in corporate finance because it reflects the overall wealth creation capacity of an organization and the perception of investors in the capital market. In the banking sector, firm value is particularly important due to its role in financial intermediation, economic stability, and investor confidence. This study examined the effect of financial attributes on the value of listed deposit money banks in Nigeria. The study focused on profitability, liquidity, leverage, capital adequacy, and asset quality as key financial attributes influencing firm value. The study adopted an ex-post facto research design, and secondary data were obtained from the annual reports and audited financial statements of 14 listed deposit money banks on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX), as well as NGX fact books, covering the period from 2016 to 2024. Panel regression analysis was employed as a technique of data analysis. The results revealed that profitability, capital adequacy, and asset quality have positive and statistically significant effects on firm value (Tobin’s Q), while liquidity and leverage show negative but statistically insignificant relationships with firm value. The study concludes that financial strength indicators play a critical role in enhancing firm value and recommends that bank management focus on improving profitability, strengthening capital adequacy, and enhancing asset quality to sustain market valuation and investor confidence.

title: Assessment of the Relationship Between Circular Supply Chain Management Practices and Sustainable Performance: A Meta‐Analysis of Empirical Evidence
summary: ABSTRACT Given the growing economic, social, and environmental challenges, sustainable performance (SUSP) offers firms a viable pathway to overcome them and gain long‐term, meaningful business value. Several mechanisms, including the circular supply chain management (CSCM), are proposed to firms to achieve SUSP. However, some empirical findings have challenged this, prompting scholarly debate about the actual direction and strength of the relationship between CSCM and SUSP, thereby leaving prospective firms in a state of strategic ambiguity. To clarify the relationship, 55 empirical studies comprising over 15,000 observations and 109 effect sizes are synthesized through a psychometric, mixed‐model random‐effects meta‐analysis. The results show a positive and significant relationship, with the effect strongest in economic performance, followed by environmental performance, and weakest in social performance. A significant effect is established in most CSCM practices with SUSP dimensions. Economy type, firm size, sector, and innovation are established as significant moderators of the relationship. Findings guide managers on the CSCM practices to prioritize and inform policymakers on the contextual conditions under which the CSCM‐SUSP relationship is strongest. It advances the supply chain management (SCM) theories by clarifying the contingent and multidimensional performance effects of CSCM and resolving inconsistencies in prior findings.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Social Commerce Supply Chains: Bibliometric Analysis of Research Trends, Knowledge Clusters and Emerging Insights
summary: The integration of artificial intelligence in social commerce supply chains has reshaped global business models. These developments are by enhancing efficiency, customer engagement and data driven decision making. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of 2,103 Scopus indexed publications (2001– 2025) by VOS Viewer and R Programming to map research trends and emerging insights. Using bibliometric and scientometric techniques, the analysis identifies publication growth patterns, influential authors, leading institutions and highly cited journals It uncovers thematic clusters such as AI enabled demand forecasting, customer behaviour analytics, digital trust and sustainable supply chain practices. The findings reveal a steady research evolution with significant acceleration after 2015. This is coinciding with the rise of digital platforms and social commerce adoption. This study contributes by offering a consolidated understanding of the field’s progression and highlighting future research directions. The insights generated serve as a valuable reference for scholars, practitioners and policymakers advancing AI driven social commerce supply chains.
